briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the daily briefing by the climate change spokesperson for November 5, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis: Impacts on Daily Life and the Economy
sections.content: According to news released today, the impacts of climate change on our daily lives and economy are intensifying. Domestically, the texture of Kellogg's products has changed due to the aftermath of climate change, and the 'snap' sound has disappeared [1]. Furthermore, 'out-of-season mosquitoes' have emerged due to abnormal weather conditions [9]. Internationally, pesticide use is increasing due to climate change [93], and a study has revealed a 33% increase in damage from Tropical Cyclone Arnab [117, 119]. Moreover, costs associated with climate change are rising [111], and Bangladesh plans to demand $15.2 billion annually in climate loss and damage compensation at COP31 [116].

sections.title: 🌍 COP31 and the International Community's Call for Climate Action
sections.content: Ahead of the upcoming COP31 UN Climate Summit, discussions on climate action within the international community are active [87, 89, 97]. UN officials have stated that COP31 offers an opportunity to translate climate commitments into action [98], while the UC San Diego delegation will address marine science [91], and the International Labour Organization (ILO) will focus on climate action for people and jobs as a key agenda item [95]. In South Korea, Minister Kim Sung-hwan held a video conference with Australia's Minister for Climate Change and Energy [3], and discussions on GEPA among South Korea, Singapore, and New Zealand have progressed, establishing a trade direction for climate change response [8]. Meanwhile, the opinion has also been raised that the EU carbon tax could present an opportunity for clean technology cooperation between Indian and German companies [121].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic Carbon Neutrality Implementation and Transition to a Hydrogen Economy
sections.content: Various domestic organizations are accelerating their efforts to achieve the 2050 carbon neutrality goal. The Korea National Railway Corporation (KNR) has become the first SOC public institution to declare participation in SBTi (Science Based Targets initiative), officially commencing its carbon neutrality practices [13, 15, 16, 17, 30, 36, 43, 46]. Furthermore, Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP) discussed its global clean hydrogen strategy, emphasizing the 2050 carbon neutrality target [18, 35, 41], and Chungcheongnam-do Province and Buyeo-gun County have completed hydrogen charging facilities, taking their first step towards establishing a hydrogen ecosystem [23, 40, 42]. Korea East-West Power (EWP) has raised its greenhouse gas reduction target to 79% by 2040 [22], and local efforts are also continuing, with Bonghwa-gun County being selected for the Carbon Neutral Agriculture and Rural RE100 demonstration project [21, 33].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Increased Investment in Eco-friendly Technologies
sections.content: There is much positive news in the renewable energy sector. With the Democratic Party's landslide victory in the U.S. midterm elections, expectations for the new and renewable energy industry are growing [49, 58, 71, 74], and the activities of domestic and international investment companies are also vigorous. Gurin Energy has reaffirmed its commitment to investing in South Korea's renewable energy sector and is pursuing K-solar and wind power development projects [50, 55, 73, 77]. Korea East-West Power (EWP) is collaborating with Goyang City to promote renewable energy and expand solar power generation [51, 57, 59, 62, 63, 64, 65, 76, 78]. Korea Southern Power (KOSPO) received a ministerial award in recognition of its contributions to renewable energy investment and green finance activation, and invested 100 billion KRW in green bonds for offshore wind power projects [52, 79, 80]. Furthermore, a preliminary feasibility study for a 1.2 trillion KRW 'artificial sun' research facility in Naju has finally passed, signaling a green light for future energy technology development [28].

sections.title: 📰 Climate Change Adaptation and Raising Social Awareness
sections.content: Adaptation efforts and activities to raise social awareness regarding climate change are also steadily progressing. Farmers in the Hwaseong region are changing their crops to kiwis in response to climate change [5], and Japan's Sapporo Breweries has conducted 30 years of research on beer barley that adapts to climate change [6]. Domestically, Gyeongsangnam-do Province held carbon neutrality and green growth awareness education to enhance climate crisis response capabilities [44, 45], and Bonghwa provided carbon neutrality practice experiences through an energy camp for youth [29]. Furthermore, the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication (YPCCC) is providing international public opinion data on climate change for Fall 2026 [88], and the opinion has been put forward that children can be taught about climate change without anxiety or guilt [99].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing. We ask for your continued interest and participation in climate change response and adaptation efforts. Thank you.
